ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the regular hexagon ABCDEF is inscribed in $\odot O$, where the radius of $\odot O$ is 1. What is the length of the apothem $OM$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OB, \\
$\because$ hexagon ABCDEF is a regular hexagon inscribed in $\odot$ O, \\
$\therefore \angle$BOM = $\frac{360^\circ}{6\times 2}$ = $30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ OM = OB $\cdot \cos \angle$BOM = 1 $\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ = $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with hexagon ABCDEF inscribed in the circle; point O is marked near the center of the circle, point M is located on the bottom side AB, and segment OM connects from O downward to M, representing the apothem of the hexagon to side AB. Reasoning: The problem gives that ABCDEF is a regular hexagon inscribed in circle O, and the circle radius is 1, so OA and OB are both radii, OB = 1. A regular hexagon divides the central angle equally into 6 parts, therefore ∠AOB = 360°/6 = 60°. The apothem OM is perpendicular to side AB, and in isosceles triangle AOB it also bisects the vertex angle, so ∠MOB = 30°. In right triangle OMB, OB is the hypotenuse and OB = 1, therefore OM = OB·cos 30° = 1·√3/2 = √3/2.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that O is the center of the circumscribed circle and M lies on side AB with OM drawn as the apothem, perpendicular to AB. From the text, the hexagon ABCDEF is regular and inscribed in a circle of radius 1, so OA and OB are radii of length 1. Since a regular hexagon divides the circle into 6 equal central angles, angle AOB is 60 degrees; the apothem to side AB bisects this angle, giving angle MOB = 30 degrees. Use right triangle OMB with hypotenuse OB = 1: OM = OB cos 30 degrees = sqrt(3)/2.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify triangle OAB, where O is the circle center and M is the foot of the apothem on side AB. From the text, the hexagon is regular and the circle radius is 1, so OA = OB = 1. In a regular inscribed hexagon, adjacent vertices subtend 60 degrees, so triangle OAB is equilateral; therefore AB = 1 as well. The apothem OM is the altitude of this equilateral triangle, meeting AB at its midpoint M. Thus AM = MB = 1/2, and in right triangle OMB, OM = sqrt(OB^2 - MB^2) = sqrt(1 - 1/4) = sqrt(3)/2.
